name: Introduction to Data Protection Law
description:
The following technical contents are taught in the module:
Chapter 1: History of data protection law and constitutional background
Chapter 2: Classification and scope of data protection law
1. systematics
2. scope of application of the German and European data protection law
3. relevant actors in data protection law
Chapter 3: Basic principles of data protection law
1. overview
2. legality
3. transparency
4. earmarking
5. data minimization
6. accountability principle
Chapter 4: Permissibility of the processing of personal data
1. legal bases of data processing according to the DSGVO
2. consent of the person concerned
3. contractual relations
4. fulfilment of legal obligations
5. protection of vital interests
6. performance of public tasks
7. predominant interest of the data processor
8. special categories of personal data
Chapter 5: Rights of data subjects
1. general information
2. information duties of the responsible person and right of access of the data subject
3. right of rectification
4. cancellation claim of the person concerned ("right to be forgotten")
5. data portability
6. right of objection and automated individual case decisions
Chapter 6: Organizational duties of the responsible person
1. strengthening of the organizational duties by the DSGVO
2. dependence of the scope of obligations on the risk of processing
3. data protection through technology design and data protection-friendly presettings
4. data security
5. message of "data mishaps
6. data protection impact assessment
7. processing list)
8. appointment of a data protection officer
9. summary
Chapter 7: Transfer of personal data abroad
1. general information
2. two-step test
3. adequacy decision of the EU
4th EU-US Privacy Shield
5. appropriate guarantees 
6. exceptions for certain cases
Chapter 8: Sanctions for data protection violations
1. overview: Data protection violations and data protection offences
2. fines for violations of data protection regulations
3. sanctions for data protection offences
4. offences under general criminal law
Chapter 9: Practical examples
1. data protection on the Internet: Case study
2. data protection on the Internet: Cookies
3. data protection in the employment relationship: case study
4. admissibility of a corona tracing app
